purpose: Resolve whether a bounded objective change from the currently best uniform-sampled pairwise logistic ranker is justified after the factorization-machine and hard-negative variants underperformed, given that the fixed primary metric averages GAUC and nDCG@5.
query: Learning-to-rank objectives for within-user logged-impression recommendation with binary relevance: compare pairwise logistic/RankNet against listwise top-k objectives (LambdaRank, LambdaMART, soft nDCG); emphasize when listwise methods improve nDCG@5 without degrading AUC under sparse per-user candidate sets and categorical ID/context features.

purpose: Resolve whether the severe tab-specific nDCG@5 gaps, especially in large tab 0 and tab 6 slices, warrant a ranking-model experiment or should first be attributed to candidate-set composition, exposure bias, or low label prevalence through non-model diagnostic analysis.
query: Offline recommender evaluation and experiment-design literature for diagnosing poor context-specific ranking in logged impression data: distinguish ranker error from candidate-inventory limitations, exposure/label-prevalence differences, and sparse segment uncertainty; focus on actionable analyses that retain fixed temporal holdout metrics and do not use post-impression outcomes as features.
